examples.en: In autumn I picked apples at an orchard.
My grandfather runs a small orchard.
Pear trees stand in rows in the orchard.

examples.ko: 과수원 주인이 갓 딴 복숭아를 주셨어요.
examples.en: The orchard owner gave me peaches just picked.
In spring the orchard is full of white flowers.
We went on a field trip to an orchard.

explain: 채소를 키우는 곳은 '밭', 쌀을 키우는 곳은 '논', 과일나무를 키우는 곳은 과수원이에요. 일하는 사람은 '과수원을 하다', 과일을 따는 일은 '따다'와 같이 써요.

phrases.example: 할머니 댁 옆에 사과 과수원이 있어요.
phrases.en: There is an apple orchard next to my grandmother's house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 과일을 키우는지 앞에 넣어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the fruit name before it to say what is grown.

phrases.en: The orchard owner shared apples with us.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the person who owns the orchard.

phrases.en: On weekends I go to the orchard with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과일을 따러 가는 곳으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for a place you go to pick fruit.

explain_en: A place for vegetables is a '밭', for rice a '논', and for fruit trees a 과수원. The owner says '과수원을 하다' (run an orchard), and picking fruit uses '따다'.

examples.ko: 서울에서 동북쪽으로 한 시간쯤 가면 공원이 나와요.
examples.en: If you go northeast from Seoul for about an hour, you reach a park.
The typhoon is slowly moving toward the northeast.
Our school is northeast of City Hall.
Morning sunlight comes in through the northeast window.
According to the compass, that mountain is to the northeast.
The sky in the northeast is full of clouds.

explain: 일상에서는 '동북쪽'과 '북동쪽'을 둘 다 써요. 가는 방향은 '동북쪽으로', 있는 위치는 '동북쪽에'로 말해요. 반대 방향은 '서남쪽'이에요.

phrases.en: My house is northeast of the school.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 동북쪽, and both are used.

phrases.en: The bus goes toward the northeast.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 으로 when talking about the direction of travel.

phrases.en: That park is in the northeast of downtown.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 에 when saying where something is.

explain_en: In daily life both '동북쪽' and '북동쪽' are used. Use '동북쪽으로' for the direction you go and '동북쪽에' for where something is. The opposite direction is '서남쪽'.

examples.en: There are empty seats at the back of the bus.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 뒷부분이 앞부분보다 더 재미있어요.
examples.en: In this movie, the last part is more fun than the first part.
I have not read the last part of the book yet.

examples.ko: 저 건물 뒷부분에 작은 주차장이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small parking lot at the back of that building.
I fell yesterday, so the back of my head hurts.
I forgot the end of the story, so I looked it up again.

explain: 반대말은 '앞부분'이에요. 공간만 말할 때는 '뒤쪽'도 자주 써요. 뒷부분은 [뒤뿌분]으로 읽고, '뒤'와 '부분' 사이에 사이시옷이 들어가요.

phrases.en: The first part of this book is a little boring.

phrases.nuance_ko: 공간을 말할 때 '뒷부분' 대신 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common alternative to 뒷부분 when talking about space.

phrases.en: I haven't read the last part of the book yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책이나 이야기의 끝쪽을 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for the end of a book or story.

explain_en: The opposite is '앞부분' (front part). For plain space, '뒤쪽' (the back side) is also common. 뒷부분 is read [뒤뿌분], with a 사이시옷 (ㅅ) between '뒤' and '부분'.

examples.en: Please turn right at the next traffic circle.

examples.ko: 로터리를 한 바퀴 돌고 나서야 길을 찾았어요.
examples.en: I only found the road after going around the traffic circle once.

examples.ko: 아침마다 로터리 앞에서 차가 많이 막혀요.
examples.en: Every morning the traffic backs up a lot in front of the traffic circle.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 시청 앞 로터리 근처예요.
examples.en: My house is near the traffic circle in front of City Hall.
There is a big fountain in the middle of the traffic circle.
Is the meeting place the cafe across from the traffic circle?

explain: '시청 앞 로터리'처럼 장소 이름 뒤에 붙여 길 이름처럼 부르기도 해요. 도로 안내에서는 '회전교차로'라는 말도 써요. '로터리를 돌다'처럼 움직임을 나타내는 말과 자주 함께 나와요.

phrases.example: 로터리를 돌아서 첫 번째 길로 가세요.
phrases.en: Go around the traffic circle and take the first road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '돌다'와 함께 운전 방향을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 돌다 it is used to give driving directions.

phrases.en: Please let me off in front of the traffic circle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 택시나 약속 장소를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for taxis or meeting places.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the traffic circle

phrases.en: Let's meet at the traffic circle in front of City Hall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소 이름과 함께 길 이름처럼 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with a place name like a street name.

explain_en: People often attach it to a place name, as in '시청 앞 로터리', and use it like a road name. In road guidance the term '회전교차로' is also used. It often pairs with movement verbs, as in '로터리를 돌다'.

examples.ko: 국내선 탑승구가 어디예요? — 이 층 오른쪽에 있어요.
examples.en: Where is the domestic flight gate? — It's on this floor, on the right.

examples.ko: 탑승구가 바뀌었으니 안내 방송을 잘 들으세요.
examples.en: The gate has changed, so listen carefully to the announcements.

examples.ko: 비행기 출발 삼십 분 전에 탑승구에 도착하세요.
examples.en: Please arrive at the boarding gate thirty minutes before departure.
I'm waiting for my family in front of the gate.

examples.ko: 저쪽 탑승구는 아직 문이 닫혀 있어요.
examples.en: The gate over there is still closed.
It takes about ten minutes to walk to the gate.

explain: 공항에서 비행기에 타는 문이에요. 번호를 붙여 '십이 번 탑승구'처럼 말하고, 공항에서는 '게이트'라고 말하는 경우도 있어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 번호를 붙여서 위치를 말하는 가장 흔한 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to name a gate by number.

phrases.nuance_ko: 공항에서 '탑승구'를 말할 때 많이 쓰는 영어식 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The English-style word often used at airports instead of 'tapseunggu'.

phrases.en: I waited for my friend in front of the boarding gate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만날 곳이나 기다릴 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name a meeting or waiting spot.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the boarding gate

explain_en: It is the door at the airport where you board the plane. You attach a number, as in '십이 번 탑승구' (gate 12), and at airports people sometimes just say '게이트'.
